data.title: Etretinate
data.summary: Retinoids · Second-generation (mono-aromatic) retinoid — ethyl ester prodrug of acitretin (withdrawn)
data.body:
_More from Khopkar · Retinoids_

**Class:** Second-generation (mono-aromatic) retinoid — ethyl ester prodrug of acitretin (withdrawn)

## Mechanism of action
- Converted to acitretin; acts on RAR/RXR like other retinoids

## Pharmacokinetics
- Highly lipophilic, stored in fat; terminal half-life 80–160 days; detected in blood up to 2–3 years after stopping

## Indications in dermatology & STI
- Formerly: psoriasis, disorders of keratinisation — replaced by acitretin (withdrawn from the US market in 1998)

## Dose & formulations
- Historic: 0.5–1 mg/kg/day

## Adverse effects
- As for acitretin (mucocutaneous, lipids, liver, bone, teratogenicity) — prolonged teratogenic risk

## Contraindications
- Pregnancy for years after stopping

## Pregnancy & lactation
Contraindicated; prolonged teratogenicity.

## Viva points
- Acitretin + alcohol → etretinate (re-esterification) — the reason for 3-year contraception with acitretin

_Sources: Wolverton 4e ch.22; Khopkar (Etretinate and acitretin). Facts summarised in our own words; Wolverton followed where books differ._
